## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Restore the federated-rule check in `useAllAlertRuleAbilities`

Affected:
- public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:222-248

Explanation:
`useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule: CombinedRule)` now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`. That function hard-codes `const isFederated = false;` and has a `// TODO` for federated support.

The old implementation called `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`, so federated Mimir rule groups were treated as immutable. All existing (V1) consumers that still pass a `CombinedRule` will now get Update, Delete and Pause abilities for federated rules. This is a silent permission/UX regression, and the backend will reject those operations.

Fix: keep the federated check for the `CombinedRule` path. Either pass a flag or group into `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, or compute it in the wrapper and override the affected abilities.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
export function useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule: CombinedRule): Abilities<AlertRuleAction> {
  const groupIdentifierV2 = useMemo(() => groupIdentifier.fromCombinedRule(rule), [rule]);
  const abilities = useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2);
  const isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group);
  return useMemo(() => {
    if (!isFederated) {
      return abilities;
    }
    const immutable = (a: Ability): Ability => [NotSupported, a[1]];
    return {
      ...abilities,
      [AlertRuleAction.Update]: immutable(abilities[AlertRuleAction.Update]),
      [AlertRuleAction.Delete]: immutable(abilities[AlertRuleAction.Delete]),
      // ...Pause, Restore, DeletePermanently
    };
  }, [abilities, isFederated]);
}
~~~

## 2) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Restore the `key` prop on mapped `GrafanaRuleListItem` in `FilterView`

Affected:
- public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/FilterView.tsx:157-162

Explanation:
The previous `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} .../>` had a `key`. The replacement `<GrafanaRuleListItem>` dropped it, even though it is rendered inside a list `map`.

The consequences are:
- React key warnings.
- Index-based reconciliation, so component state (menus, drawers, modals) can attach to the wrong rule when the filtered list changes or more rules are loaded.

Proposed fix:
~~~tsx
<GrafanaRuleListItem
  key={key}
  rule={rule}
  groupIdentifier={groupIdentifier}
  namespaceName={ruleWithOrigin.namespaceName}
  showLocation={true}
/>
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Base Pause/Restore/Export abilities on "Grafana rule", not only "alerting rule"

Affected:
- public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:301-330

Explanation:
The Ruler-based version gated these actions on `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which is true for every Grafana-managed rule, including recording rules. The new Prom-based version uses `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` for all of the following:
- `ModifyExport`
- `Pause`
- `Restore`
- `DeletePermanently`

As a result, Grafana-managed recording rules lose pause, restore and export from the list view. The comment on line 301 ("All GrafanaPromRuleDTO rules are Grafana-managed") contradicts how the variable is used.

Only Silence should be limited to alerting rules.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const isGrafanaManagedRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule);
const isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule);
...
[AlertRuleAction.Silence]: [silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule],
[AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport]: [isGrafanaManagedRule, exportAllowed],
[AlertRuleAction.Pause]: [MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isGrafanaManagedRule, isEditable ?? false],
[AlertRuleAction.Restore]: [MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isGrafanaManagedRule, isEditable ?? false],
[AlertRuleAction.DeletePermanently]: [MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isGrafanaManagedRule, (isRemovable && isAdmin()) ?? false],
~~~

## 4) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Implementation
Title: Pause/Delete computed from `promRule` likely never render without `rulerRule`; the test locks this in

Affected:
- public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:81-100
- public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx:191-207

Explanation:
`canPause` and `canDelete` can now be true from the Prom-only abilities. However, the list view no longer passes `rulerRule`.

The new test grants `AlertingRuleDelete` and `AlertingRuleUpdate` but asserts exactly 4 menu items (silence, copy link, duplicate, export). That means neither Delete nor Pause appears even though the user is permitted. This suggests the menu items, or the delete-modal and pause handlers in `RuleActionsButtons.V2`, still require a `RulerRuleDTO`. The rendering code is outside this diff, so I cannot confirm it directly.

Net effect: users lose Delete and Pause from the new list view without any indication. Either wire these actions to work with `promRule` (fetch the ruler rule on demand), or document the limitation explicitly. The test should assert the intended behavior rather than an exact count that hides the missing actions.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
// test: be explicit about expected availability
expect(ui.menuItems.delete().query()).toBeInTheDocument(); // or .not, with a comment explaining why
~~~

## 5) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Security
Title: Provisioned-rule immutability now depends on `provenance` being returned by the Prometheus API

Affected:
- public/app/types/unified-alerting-dto.ts:135
- public/app/features/alerting/unified/utils/rules.ts:171-173
- public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:296

Explanation:
`isProvisionedPromRule` reads `promRule.provenance`, which this change only adds as an optional TypeScript field. No backend change is part of this diff.

If the Grafana Prom-compatible rules endpoint does not populate `provenance`, every provisioned rule will appear mutable in the list view. Edit, Delete and Pause would then be offered for rules that must not be changed through the UI, and the "provisioned" badge would disappear. This depends on backend code not visible here.

Fix: verify that the endpoint serializes `provenance`, and add a test using a provisioned Prom rule.

Proposed fix:
~~~text
- Confirm the backend /api/prometheus/grafana/api/v1/rules response includes `provenance`.
- Add a GrafanaGroupLoader test with provenance: 'file' asserting no Edit button and no Delete/Pause.
~~~

## 6) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: Restore `returnTo` on the rule view link

Affected:
- public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:40

Explanation:
The deleted implementation built the link as `createRelativeUrl(..., { returnTo: createReturnTo() })`. The new component drops `returnTo`.

Navigating from the list to a rule's detail page and back now loses the list's filter and scroll context. This is a UX regression that is not mentioned in the PR's intent.

Proposed fix:
~~~tsx
const returnTo = createReturnTo();
...
href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo }),
~~~

## 7) Severity: LOW | Type: Performance
Title: Plural ability hooks memoize on an inline array, so the memo is ineffective

Affected:
- public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:397-406
- public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:57-79

Explanation:
`AlertRuleMenu` passes a new array literal of actions on every render. Because `useMemo(..., [abilities, actions])` depends on that array, it recomputes every time and returns a new array, so downstream consumers see new references on every render.

In addition, every list item now runs both the ruler and Prom ability computations. That includes `useFolder` and `useIsRuleEditable` for each list item. On large lists this adds work for no benefit.

Fix: hoist the action arrays to module-level constants, and skip the ruler hook entirely when no `rulerRule` is provided.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const MENU_ACTIONS = [
  AlertRuleAction.Pause,
  AlertRuleAction.Delete,
  AlertRuleAction.Duplicate,
  AlertRuleAction.Silence,
  AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport,
] as const;
// ...
useRulerRuleAbilities(rulerRule, groupIdentifier, MENU_ACTIONS);
useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) ? promRule : skipToken, MENU_ACTIONS);
~~~

true_positives.matched_candidate: GrafanaRuleListItem in FilterView is missing the key prop that was present on the previous GrafanaRuleLoader, causing React key warnings and potential state attachment to wrong rules when filtered list changes
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment: the GrafanaRuleListItem component is missing the required key prop for React list items. Pause/Restore/Export abilities are gated on prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule instead of prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule, causing Grafana-managed recording rules to lose pause, restore and export capabilities

canPause and canDelete can be true from Prom-only abilities but the list view no longer passes rulerRule, and the test asserts exactly 4 menu items hiding that Delete and Pause actions are missing for permitted users
isProvisionedPromRule reads promRule.provenance but no backend change ensures the Prometheus API returns this field, potentially making provisioned rules appear mutable in the list view
The returnTo parameter was dropped from the rule view link, causing navigation from list to rule detail and back to lose filter and scroll context

false_negatives.golden_comment: RuleActionsButtons is invoked with only promRule, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer inside RuleActionsButtons still depends on a Grafana Ruler rule being present, so for Grafana rules coming from list views the 'Silence notifications' menu entry (now driven by Grafana Prom abilities) will toggle showSilenceDrawer without ever rendering the drawer. This means clicking 'Silence notifications' for these rules has no visible effect, even when abilities indicate silencing is allowed.
